competitors.name: Kroger
competitors.action: Grocery Dive reported Kroger will run wellness-focused in-store activations every Friday and Saturday in September and host larger community mini-fests in the Houston, Phoenix, Salt Lake City and Nashville areas. Events include better-for-you product sampling, OptUP Picks, pharmacist and dietitian access, cooking demonstrations, coupons and wellness workshops.

competitors.name: Amazon Grocery
competitors.action: Progressive Grocer reported Amazon Grocery launched a Spend Less on Your Groceries campaign with actress Kathryn Hahn. Amazon is positioning grocery as a value-and-convenience service with fresh and household essentials in the same cart, free same-day delivery over $25 for Prime members, and more than 1,000 Amazon Grocery private-label products mostly priced under $5.

competitors.name: Dollar General / RELEX Solutions
competitors.action: Progressive Grocer reported Dollar General is deploying RELEX Solutions' AI-driven forecasting, replenishment and allocation platform across North American operations. The system will manage store replenishment, ordering schedules, lead times, supplier coordination and fulfillment methods for a retailer with more than 21,000 stores, 34 distribution centers and about 18,000 SKUs.

trends.topic: Health and wellness moving into in-store grocery activation
trends.magnitude: Kroger plans weekly September activations plus four metro-area mini-fests.
trends.context: Better-for-you frozen and prepared products will increasingly be merchandised through sampling, dietitian/pharmacy adjacency and retailer health platforms, not only through package claims.

trends.topic: E-grocery value messaging tightening around private label and low delivery thresholds
trends.magnitude: Amazon Grocery cited more than 1,000 private-label products, most under $5, and free same-day delivery over $25 for Prime members.
trends.context: Premium CPG brands need a clear reason to win search and basket placement when e-grocery platforms lead with private-label affordability and convenience.

trends.topic: AI replenishment expectations spreading into value retail
trends.magnitude: Dollar General is adding AI planning across more than 21,000 stores, 34 distribution centers and roughly 18,000 SKUs.
trends.context: Retail buyers are moving toward more data-driven ordering and allocation; frozen brands need dependable item data, availability and supply coordination to stay competitive.
